answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded): The type of plant introduction most influenced by urban land use is the UNINTENTIONAL pathway (accidental introductions via contaminated seed lots, global trade, and tourism), with the GARDENING pathway (ornamental/medicinal cultivation) showing a strong but secondary positive urban association, while the AGRIFOREST (agriculture/forestry) pathway is essentially unassociated with urban land cover.

Data support (plot-level: 632 plots in Barcelona province, 191 with >=1 non-native species; each pathway's species count modeled against urban land cover at 3 years x 3 buffers):

1) Direct association (univariate Poisson, the primary evidence for "influenced by urban land use"): every pathway's species count rises with urban cover. The Unintentional pathway has the STRONGEST positive urban slope in ALL 9 year x buffer cells (mean ~+0.37 log-count per 1-SD urban ~ +44% on average). At 2009/500 m, a 1-SD increase in urban cover -> ~+70% expected Unintentional count vs ~+55% Gardening and ~+17% AgriForest. Gardening is consistently 2nd (positive in 9/9 cells, mean ~+0.31 ~ +37%); AgriForest is weakest (positive in 7/9 cells, mean ~+0.09 ~ +9%, and negative at some scales).

2) Temporal: the urban association STRENGTHENS toward the most recent year (2009 > 1993 > 1956) for all pathways, indicating recent urbanization is the relevant driver.

3) Descriptive (dominant-pathway, 191 occupied plots): plots where Unintentional species dominate sit in the most urban surroundings (mean 2009 urban cover 0.33 at 500 m; n=134) vs 0.26 for Gardening-dominant (n=79) and 0.16 for AgriForest-dominant (n=10, low precision).

4) Robustness: the ordering Unintentional > Gardening > AgriForest holds across every buffer (50/500/1000 m) and every year; Unintentional is the max in 9/9 cells.

Ecological reading: urban areas (trade, transport, tourism, disturbed ground, gardens) are the source/sink for accidentally introduced and ornamental species, whereas agriculture/forestry species track rural cropland and are therefore not urban-associated.

payload.hypothesis: Urban land use most strongly and consistently influences UNINTENTIONAL plant introductions (accidental, via contaminated seed, global trade, tourism), with a strong secondary positive effect on GARDENING (ornamental) introductions and little to no effect on AGRIFOREST (agriculture/forestry) introductions. The Unintentional pathway shows the strongest positive urban association in all 9 year x buffer cells (mean ~+44% expected species count per 1-SD urban; ~+70% at 2009/500 m), the association strengthens toward 2009, and Unintentional-dominant plots sit in the most urban surroundings (mean 2009 urban cover 0.33 vs 0.26 Gardening, 0.16 AgriForest).
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots x 37 cols, tab-separated; urban vars are 0-1 proportions). 2) Descriptive dominant-pathway comparison on the 191 occupied plots (plots where each pathway is argmax of n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo), reporting n per pathway and mean 2009 urban cover at 50/500/1000 m. 3) Primary Poisson GLM per pathway: count ~ urban.2009.500m + habitat + elevation + cropland.2009.500m + distance.road + distance.stream + climate; reported raw coef, 95% CI, p, and standardized (log-count change per 1-SD urban = coef x SD). 4) Sensitivity grid: univariate Poisson per pathway for all 9 urban year x buffer columns; identified the pathway with the max standardized urban slope per cell and sign consistency. 5) Permutation Moran's I (999 perms, 10-NN weights) on adjusted-model Pearson residuals to check spatial autocorrelation. Pathway with the strongest, most consistent positive urban association = most influenced by urban land use.
